newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wary Australian stocks drift to just lower close.
newsitem.headline: Wary Australian stocks drift to just lower close.

text.p: SPI Futures 2488 -8 US 30yr cl 6.96 -0.02
10yrbond futs 92.040 -0.090 Gold NY 339.55 Lon fix 340.15
*Stocks drift to end barely lower after day of choppy trade, bonds weigh, wary eye on U.S. Volume 345.38 million, A$731.16 million, 1,044 stocks traded, 323 steady, 317 up, 404 down.
Local indecision and persistent nervousness over Wall Street's behaviour pushed the Australian share market just lower by the close on Thursday.
The All Ordinaries index lost 2.6 points to 2,485.4.
June share price index futures were down eight points at 2,488, a 2.6 point premium to the underlying index.

Continued scepticism over Wall Street's rebound, with key economic data still to come in the U.S., compounded by stronger than expected local wages data saw the market endure a day of choppy, rangebound trade with little real direction.

"On the face of it, it's a disappointing performance after Wall Street rose again last night, although it was partly flagged yesterday by the way we came off our highs yesterday," said Steve Mayne, dealer at Brisbane brokerage, Nevitts Ltd.
"The market just showed how nervous it was regarding this U.S. market with figures still coming out there."
The market drifted, with two distinct ranges to which it was tethered all day. Any trend proved elusive.
"It's just been drifting and has traded in a very narrow range, only up or down five points or so the whole day," Mayne said.
The leaders epitomised this patchy display, with bellwether BHP traversing a 20 cent range only to end unchanged at A$18.08 while News Corp added two to end at A$5.93.

Among others, gold miner Newcrest Mining was savaged after its A$7.1 million March quarter net loss reported on Wednesday. Its shares hit A$3.48, their lowest level since September 1993, before clawing back some ground to end 7.3 percent lower at A$3.53.
Drug developer Cortecs International, added 22 cents to A$5.82 in thin trade as it awaited test results for its 'Macritonin' osteoporosis treatment, due by May 2.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about five to four, while about 31 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Options and futures markets saw only moderate trade with the same patchy activity seen in underlying markets.
Total options traded 31,294 (48,144)
Turnover in June SPI contracts totalled 6,248 (10,451)
In other local markets, the Australian dollar rose across the board after disturbingly strong domestic wage data made it far less likely official rates would be cut soon.
By 4.55 p.m. (0655 GMT), the local dollar had climbed to USS$0.7843/48 from an early US$0.7808/13 and US$0.7813/18 late here Wednesday.
Australian debt sold off sharply following the wages report, which eroded hopes of any early easing in monetary policy and brought forward expectations of a tightening this year.
The benchmark November 2006 bond yield ended some 15 basis points higher than its initial U.S.-led lows on the data and by 4.55 p.m. (0655 GMT) was yielding 7.94 percent.
